not std::os::unix::raw::gid_t (already covered, resolves to u32 via std's own rustdoc index) -- a distinct occurrence surfaced by SocketCred::get_gid/set_gid's signatures in std::os::unix::net::ancillary, which reference libc::gid_t directly. libc is never given its own rustdoc pass by the coverage pipeline (only std/core/alloc are), so std's rustdoc JSON only carries a bare paths-table stub for this id -- {crate_id, path, kind}, no type information at all -- and libc::gid_t's real definition (u32, confirmed by reading libc 0.2.189's own src/unix/mod.rs) can't be recovered from that. The value is the same u32 either way and is already proven; this is a rustdoc-metadata artifact for an un-rustdoc'd external crate, not a missing proof. Same reasoning for pid_t (i32) and uid_t (u32).
